eyewitness reporter of Rav Kahana's practice (10a.2)

וחד אמר -- the other of R' Yirmeya and R' Yona

תנו רבנן, the mealtimes baraita (10a.7), emended at 10a.8
the מיתיבי source at 10a.9-11 on the three rooms of a bathhouse
anonymous redactorial voice of this unit

props.gloss_en: a person may not sit before the barber near minchah until he prays; nor enter the bathhouse, the tannery, to eat, or to judge
and if they began, they do not stop
'near minchah' in the mishnah is near minchah gedola
rather, [the mishnah means] near minchah ketana
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: once the time of the minchah prayer has arrived, a person may not taste anything before he prays minchah
the activities are: Ben Elasa's haircut; the whole business of the bath; a big tannery; a big meal; the beginning of a trial
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: actually even our ordinary haircut; the bath just to sweat; the tannery just to look; a small meal; the end of a trial
why may he not sit [for a haircut] ab initio? a decree lest the scissors break
why not [enter the bathhouse] ab initio? a decree lest he faint
why not [enter the tannery] ab initio? lest he see a loss in his wares and be preoccupied
why not [begin a small meal] ab initio? lest he come to prolong it
why not [enter to judge, even at the end] ab initio? lest he see a reason and overturn the verdict
Rav Avin: the haircut begins when he places the barbers' wrap on his knees
Rav Avin: the bath begins when he removes his cloak
the tannery [work] begins when he ties [the apron] between his shoulders
Rav: eating begins when he washes his hands
R' Chanina: eating begins when he loosens his belt
and they do not disagree: this is for us, and that is for them
Abaye: these Babylonian scholars -- according to the one who says the evening prayer is optional, once he has loosened his belt we do not trouble him [to stop and pray]
Abaye: and according to the one who says it is obligatory, we trouble him
because it is said: 'prepare to greet your God, Israel' (Amos 4:12)
Rava bar Rav Huna would put on fine socks and pray
Rava bar Rav Huna said: 'prepare to greet [your God, Israel]'
Rava would throw off his cloak, clasp his hands, and pray
Rava said: as a slave before his master
Rav Ashi: I saw Rav Kahana, when there was distress in the world, throw off his cloak, clasp his hands and pray
Rav Kahana said: as a slave before his master
Rav Ashi: when there was peace, [Rav Kahana] would dress, cover and wrap himself, and pray
Rav Kahana said: 'prepare to greet your God, Israel'
Rava, seeing Rav Hamnuna prolong his prayer: they leave eternal life and engage in temporal life
and he [Rav Hamnuna] held: the time for prayer is apart and the time for Torah is apart
R' Zeira read over R' Yirmeya, who was hurrying [to pray] as the time for prayer came: 'one who turns his ear from hearing Torah, even his prayer is an abomination' (Prov 28:9)
one said: judgment begins when the judges wrap themselves
the other said: judgment begins when the litigants open [their pleas]
and they do not disagree: this is where they were already engaged in judgment, that where they were not
Rav Ami and Rav Asi would sit and study between the pillars, and every hour knock on the door-bolt and say: if anyone has a case, let him come in
Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna would sit in judgment all day, and their hearts grew faint
(entertained) that Moses sat and judged the whole day -- then when was his Torah [study] done?

rather, to tell you: any judge who judges a true judgment truthfully, even for one hour, Scripture accounts it to him as though he became a partner of the Holy One, blessed be He, in the work of creation
Rav Sheshet: they sit in judgment until mealtime

Rav Chama: which verse? 'woe to you, land whose king is a lad and whose ministers eat in the morning; happy are you, land whose king is free and whose ministers eat in time, in strength and not in drinking' (Eccl 10:16-17) -- in the strength of Torah and not in the drinking of wine
the first hour is the mealtime of Ludim
the second, of robbers
the third, of heirs
[as first cited:] the fourth is the mealtime of workers; the fifth, of all people
Rav Pappa: the fourth [hour] is mealtime for all people
rather [read]: the fourth is the mealtime of all people
the fifth, of workers
the sixth, of Torah scholars
from then on -- like one throwing a stone into a flask
Abaye: we said this only where he tasted nothing in the morning; but if he tasted something in the morning, we have no concern
Rav Adda bar Ahava: a person may pray his prayer in the bathhouse
one who enters a bathhouse: where people stand dressed, there is reading [of Torah] and prayer there, and all the more greeting; and he dons tefillin, and all the more does not remove them
where people stand naked and dressed, there is greeting there but no reading or prayer; he does not remove tefillin, and does not don them ab initio
where people stand naked, there is no greeting there, and all the more no reading or prayer; he removes tefillin, and all the more does not don them
when Rav Adda bar Ahava said it, [he meant] a bathhouse with no one in it
R' Yosei bar Chanina: the bathhouse they spoke of -- even though there is no one in it
R' Yosei bar Chanina: the privy they spoke of -- even though there is no feces in it
rather, when Rav Adda said it, [he meant] a new one
Ravina's dilemma: if one designated [a structure] as a privy, what is the law -- is there designation or is there no designation?
no -- perhaps a privy is different, for it is disgusting

schemas.gloss_en: כתיב הכא: ויעמד העם על משה מן הבקר עד הערב (Ex 18:13), וכתיב התם: ויהי ערב ויהי בקר יום אחד (Gen 1:5) -- morning-and-evening here as morning-and-evening in the work of creation

questions.gloss_en: one who designated a structure as a privy: does designation take effect or not? ולא איפשיטא ליה -- left unresolved (no תיקו is written)

supports.gloss_en: מאי קרא -- ושריך בעת יאכלו בגבורה ולא בשתי: in the strength of Torah, and not in the drinking of wine

challenges.gloss_en: מתקיף לה רב ששת: טריחותא למיסר המייניה?! -- is it a burden to tie his belt? (no reply is given to this limb)

objections.gloss_en: אילימא למנחה גדולה -- אמאי לא? האיכא שהות ביום טובא: if the mishnah meant near minchah gedola, why not? there is plenty of day left

answered_by.gloss_en: לעולם סמוך למנחה גדולה, ובתספורת בן אלעשה... -- the activities are the long ones (= p_melachot_arukot)
לעולם בתספורת דידן; לכתחילה אמאי לא -- גזירה שמא ישבר הזוג... -- even the ordinary activities, forbidden ab initio by decree (= p_melachot_ktanot and the five reasons)

objections.gloss_en: אם התחילו אין מפסיקין -- נימא תיהוי תיובתא דרבי יהושע בן לוי: if the mishnah speaks of minchah ketana, one who began eating need not stop, against R' Yehoshua ben Levi's 'may not taste anything'

answered_by.gloss_en: לא: לעולם סמוך למנחה גדולה -- the mishnah speaks of minchah gedola (and the long activities), so it says nothing of the time of minchah ketana
רב אחא בר יעקב אמר: לעולם -- he too places the mishnah at minchah gedola

objections.gloss_en: והא תפלת מנחה דלכולי עלמא חובה היא, ותנן אם התחילו אין מפסיקין, ואמר רבי חנינא משיתיר חגורו -- minchah is obligatory for all, yet one who loosened his belt need not stop; why should obligatory arvit be different?

answered_by.gloss_en: התם לא שכיחא שכרות, הכא שכיחא שכרות -- drunkenness is uncommon there (by day), common here (at night)
אי נמי: במנחה, כיון דקביעא לה זימנא מירתת ולא אתי למפשע; ערבית, כיון דכולה ליליא זמן ערבית, לא מירתת ואתי למפשע

objections.gloss_en: ועוד, ליקו הכי וליצלי -- and moreover, let him stand as he is [unbelted] and pray

answered_by.gloss_en: משום שנאמר הכון לקראת אלהיך ישראל (= p_hikon_tefilla)

objections.gloss_en: איני?! והאמר רב פפא: רביעית זמן סעודה לכל אדם -- conceded: אלא, the baraita is re-read (fourth for all people, fifth for workers, sixth for Torah scholars)
מיתיבי: where people stand naked there is no greeting, and all the more no reading or prayer -- how may one pray in the bathhouse?

answered_by.gloss_en: כי קאמר רב אדא בר אהבה במרחץ שאין בו אדם (= p_okimta_ein_bo_adam); itself attacked and given up at 10a.13
אלא כי קאמר רב אדא בחדתי -- a new bathhouse (= p_okimta_chadtei_merchatz)

objections.gloss_en: והא אמר רבי יוסי בר חנינא: מרחץ שאמרו אף על פי שאין בו אדם -- an empty bathhouse is still the bathhouse they forbade (kind svara under protest: amoraic memra)

והא מבעא בעא ליה רבינא: הזמינו לבית הכסא מהו, יש זימון או אין זימון? ולא איפשיטא ליה -- לאו הוא הדין למרחץ? the new-bathhouse okimta seems to settle for a bathhouse what was left unresolved for a privy (source is the dilemma p_q_hazmana_beit_hakisei; no source slot for a question)

answered_by.gloss_en: לא, דילמא שאני בית הכסא דמאיס (= p_shani_beit_hakisei)
